newsitem.title: FRANCE: Sogaris poised to sign up FedEx.
newsitem.headline: Sogaris poised to sign up FedEx.

text.p: French freight installations operator, Sogaris, said it was finalising an agreement with Federal Express to occupy warehouse and office space in the extension of its existing facilties at Paris-Charles de Gaulle (CDG) airport.

"Our negotiations with FedEx centre on a letting of 900 squares metres of warehousing and 200 square metres of offices in the extension, probably to be occupied by end-June 1997," a Sogaris official told Reuters.
FedEx already occupied 1,200 square metres of warehousing at Sogaris' CDG site, dedicated to aircraft maintenance, the official said.

"The need for additional facilities at CDG in the short-term reflects our rate of a growth in traffic," a FedEx official said, adding that the U.S. express operator's existing facilites at the Paris airport covered an area of some 9,000 square metres.
The Sogaris extension, costing 60 million francs is scheduled to enter service on May 1 1997.
It will provide an extra 10,000 sq.metres of warehousing and 2,200 sq.metres of office space.
KLM subsidiary, Cargo Service Centre (CSC) said it had let dedicated facilities in the extension covering 1,350 sq.metres of warehousing and 310 sq.metres of offices.
"The extension is effectively fully-let," the Sogaris official said.

In a seperate project, construction work on FedEx's 70,000 square metre traffic hub at CDG is likely to begin towards the end of 1997 with a scheduled opening in June 1999. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax:5017
